subtitle: 表哥，你先让人把门打开
sentences: The marquis's guards stopped me at the gate. I was still wearing Wen Li's wedding gown.

Chuntao clutched the clothes she'd fetched from home, her voice rising with panic. "Miss, your mother says you must come back at once. But the whole city is talking. They say you stood in for the bride—and stole the marquis's account books!"
I looked down. I hadn't even had time to change, and the gold embroidery on my sleeves was doing nothing to help me keep a low profile.
"The first part's true. What does the second part have to do with me?"
"You think the people spreading rumors care?"

She looked ready to cry. For the first time since arriving in this world, I really looked at her. She couldn't have been more than fifteen or sixteen. Sweat shone along her hairline, and the lace on her right shoe had snapped; she'd tied it up with a strip of cloth. In the original novel, Chuntao barely appeared, yet she was sent to the family shrine along with Jiang Mingyue.
The book never bothered to say what she'd done wrong.
"Come on." I caught her hand and headed for the gate.
A guard held out his sheathed sword to block our path. "The Young Lord has ordered that his cousin remain here for now."
"Hasn't he gone to the Ministry of Punishments? Let him check his accounts. What's that got to do with me?"
"Our orders are to keep you here, Miss Jiang.
Without further instructions, we cannot let you leave."
In other words, nobody wanted to be the one who took responsibility.
I peered outside.
The Jiang family carriage was still there, with two of my aunts standing beside it.
One was Second Aunt, who could lecture the original Jiang Mingyue about manners without stopping once for air.
Wonderful. For once, she had a perfectly good reason to scold someone.
I raised my voice. "Second Aunt! The Young Lord's gone, and his guards still won't let me leave!"
She turned. Her eyelid twitched at the sight of me in red, and then her face darkened.
"Jiang Mingyue!
What have you done this time?"
"Scold me at home," I said. "First, please get me out of here."

"Since when does the Xie family get to detain an unmarried girl?" Second Aunt rounded on the guard, louder than the wedding drums. "Linzhou is away? Then fetch your steward! She put on the wrong wedding dress. Does that mean she has to spend the night here being questioned?"
The guard did not move his arm.

I took off the phoenix crown and held it against my chest. "Please pass a message to my cousin. Open the gate first; he can sort out the accounts afterward. I'm not running away. If he's worried, send someone to follow our carriage home. Surely I'm still allowed to see my mother?"
"I'll take her home myself," Second Aunt declared.
"If you need someone to answer for it, write down my name."
After a long standoff, the guards fetched a steward. He took one look at the crowd gathering outside, gritted his teeth, and stepped aside. He even sent two men to follow the carriage.
By the time I climbed in, my back was soaked with sweat.
Chuntao sat opposite me and began taking the pins out of my hair.
The third pin caught a strand, and I hissed in pain.
Her eyes filled. "Miss, the Young Lord won't really send you to the family shrine, will he?"
My stomach tightened.
"Who told you about that?"
"Last month, after you offended Miss Wen, the Young Lord mentioned it.
Madam didn't want me to hear, but I was standing outside the door."
I rubbed the red marks Xie Linzhou had left around my wrist. Suddenly, the fire waiting for me in Chapter Nineteen didn't seem so far away.
My mother, Lady Li, was waiting in the Jiang residence's main hall.
Her first words were not a scolding.
"Show me your hand."
She took my wrist. When she saw the marks, her face grew hard.
"Xie Linzhou did this?"
"He wouldn't let go."
"Did he hurt you anywhere else?"
"No."
Only then did she release me. Her eyes fell on the phoenix crown in my arms. "Who dressed you in that gown?"

Her palms carried a faint scent of herbs. Before I ended up here, my own mother had always complained that I stayed up too late. Every few days, she'd send a message asking if I was eating properly. I remembered the last message I'd never answered, and my throat tightened.
"Wen Li."
"You planned this together?"
"Yes."
"Did you know she was going to the Ministry of Punishments with a complaint?"
"No."
Mother studied me for a long moment. I was bracing for Are you out of your mind? Instead, she asked, "Chuntao says you gave her a bowl of drugged tea to keep safe. Where is it?"
I stared at her.
"How did you know it was drugged?"
"She came home crying and managed to tell me most of what you'd asked her to." Mother held out her hand. "Give it here."

Chuntao set the little cloth bag on the table. She'd carried it from the Wen residence to the wedding, and all the way back here. Inside were the sealed tea bowl, the remaining powder, and the stained handkerchief. The sight of them turned my stomach. I had almost hurt Wen Li with my own hands.
Lady Li examined the contents for a long time. At last she said, "If you had actually harmed that girl today, I couldn't have protected you. And I shouldn't have."
I lowered my head. "I know."
She asked Chuntao for a clean wooden box, wrapped and sealed the items separately, and said she'd have a physician examine them tomorrow.
Then she sent word to the Wen family: the Jiangs were prepared to apologize, and they would not destroy the evidence.
Only after that did I dare sit down.
An opened letter lay on the table.
It was signed by Xie Linzhou—and dated three days earlier.
I unfolded it. The words Beihe relief grain stared back at me, and my heart sank.

The letter was unfailingly polite. Three years ago, it said, the Jiang Trading House had helped arrange river transport for a shipment of relief grain to Beihe. If the Ministry reopened the case, Lady Li was to send all the old boat tickets and transport accounts to the marquis's residence, where Xie Linzhou would examine them himself.
"He knew three days ago?" I asked.
"He always knew our family had arranged those boats," Mother said. "I thought he was warning me. Now I suspect he wanted to get hold of the papers first."
"Did you give them to him?"
"No."
She tapped a locked wooden chest beside the table.

"The officials were desperate to move grain that year. Our family hired the boats and was paid the proper transport fee. But after the boats left, the receipts that came back from the granary didn't match. While your father was still alive, he told Accountant Song to keep copies."
"Where's Accountant Song now?"
"He died of illness last year."
Mother ran a finger over the lock.
She could silence three stewards at once when she was talking business, but her voice slowed whenever she mentioned Accountant Song.
"Twice before he died, he begged me to get rid of those papers. I couldn't bring myself to burn them. I didn't dare show them to anyone, either."
"Why not?"
"Because a single ticket can save someone—or ruin them." She looked at me. "If you hand over your piece without knowing what the other side holds, how can you tell who will suffer for it?"
I'd thought I could save Wen Li simply because I'd read a novel. Suddenly I felt rather foolish.
A servant appeared at the door. "Madam, Miss Wen is here. She's waiting at the back gate."
I shot to my feet. "She has the nerve to come here?"
Wen Li entered through the small gate beside the embroidery workshop.
She wore an ordinary, pale dress, with a fresh streak of mud on one shoe.
Our elderly gatekeeper followed several paces behind, looking even more nervous than she did.
Lady Li regarded her coolly. "Weren't you just at the Ministry of Punishments?"

"They accepted the complaint and the ledger for the record. They took my name and asked for an address where I could be summoned." Wen Li bowed properly. "I used your family's carriage to get out of the Wen residence. Two streets later, I sent the driver back and returned the carriage pass. He didn't take me to the Ministry. And I took a roundabout route before coming here."
Mother's voice was cold. "You weren't nearly so considerate when you used my daughter as a distraction."

Wen Li lowered her eyes. "I took advantage of Miss Jiang. She agreed to ride in the bridal sedan, not to keep the Young Lord occupied. She certainly didn't agree to be accused of stealing his accounts."
I'd spent the whole ride thinking of things to yell at her. Hearing her admit it so readily only made me angrier.
"Why didn't you tell me you were going to file a complaint?"
"I thought you'd refuse."
"Of course I'd have refused!"
"That's why I didn't tell you."
She raised her head and met my eyes.
"I know it was unfair. You can shout at me in a minute," Wen Li said. "But I had to come today. The ledger names the Jiang Trading House, and I didn't want you to hear about it from Xie Linzhou."
"How thoughtful of you."
"The old ledger from the marquis's residence says that, on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month, the Jiang Trading House shipped eight thousand shi of relief grain to Beihe by river."
Lady Li's expression changed. "The ninth day of the twelfth month?"
Wen Li nodded.
"Impossible," Mother said sharply. "The Beihe waterways closed at the end of the eleventh month that year. Our boats sailed on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month."
"Are those records even talking about the same shipment?" I asked.
"We don't know yet," Mother said. "That's why we need the old boat tickets and the official granary records."
She stopped abruptly, as if she'd just revealed something she'd kept hidden for three years.
Wen Li's eyes sharpened, but she made no move toward the chest.
"Lady Li, I didn't come to demand your original documents," she said. "I only want to know when the Jiang boats actually departed, and whether any other records survive."
"And drag the Jiang family before the Ministry?" Mother asked.
"The Jiang name is already in that ledger," Wen Li replied. "If we don't check the facts, other people can use it against you, and we'll have nothing to challenge them with."
They looked at each other across the table. Neither gave an inch.
I cut in. "Before we go any further: hiring boats doesn't mean our family received the grain. And it certainly doesn't mean we know where the grain ended up. Right?"
Mother turned toward me. "Of course not."

I faced Wen Li. "Your ledger only proves that someone wrote our name down. It doesn't prove our boats carried grain on that date. If we're going to investigate together, don't present a guess as a fact."
Wen Li was quiet for a moment.
"All right." She nodded. "From now on, I'll tell you what I know and what I only suspect."
Her answer was softer than before.
I wasn't ready to forgive her. "One more thing. How did that ledger get out of the marquis's study and into your hands?"
Wen Li shook her head. "I can't name the person who helped me. Their family is still inside the marquis's residence."
"You're keeping another secret from me?"
"This one I have to keep." She held my gaze. "You can refuse to help me. But I won't risk someone else's life just to win your trust."
I closed my mouth.
Mother watched Wen Li for a long while. Then she pushed the locked chest toward the middle of the table.
"Sit down."

"If we're going to talk, we'll put every account we know about on the table," she said. "Whoever is responsible will answer for it. But if anyone thinks they can buy their way out with my daughter's life, they can think again."
She drew a key from her sleeve.
The brass lock gave a soft click.
translations: 侯府的亲卫拦在门口时，我还穿着温梨的嫁衣。
春桃抱着刚从姜府取来的衣裳，急得声音都变了：“小姐，夫人让您立刻回去。可外头已经传遍了，说您替人拜堂，还偷了侯府的账！”
我低头看看自己，身上那件嫁衣还没来得及换，连袖口的金线都扎眼得很。
“前半句是对的，后半句跟我有什么关系？”
“传话的人才不管这个！”
春桃急得快哭了。我这才仔细看清她：十五六岁的年纪，额前全是细汗，右脚的鞋带断了，用布条胡乱缠着。原著里她只露过几次面，最后却跟着姜明月一起被送进家庙。
书里没交代她到底做错了什么。
“走。”我拉着她往外。
门口的亲卫横过刀鞘：“世子有令，表小姐暂且不得离府。”
“他不是去刑部了吗？查账就查账，关我什么事？”
“世子吩咐看住表小姐。
没新的命令，属下不能放人。”
说到底，就是不敢担责任。
我朝门外看去。
姜家的马车还停着，车旁站着两位方才来赴宴的姑母。
其中一位是二姑母，平日骂起原主不懂规矩，从不需要先喝口水。
救命，这位今日总算可以骂在正地方了。
我索性冲门外喊：“二姑母！世子不在，侯府还要把我扣到晚上！”
二姑母转过身，看见我一身大红，先是眼皮一跳，随后脸都青了。
“姜明月！
你又闯什么祸？”
“回家再骂。”我说，“您先把我领出去。”
“谢家凭什么扣一个未出阁的姑娘？”二姑母转向亲卫，声音比方才的锣鼓还响，“临舟不在，叫你们管事来！难不成她今日穿错了嫁衣，晚上还得留在侯府受审？”
亲卫的手仍拦着门。
我把凤冠摘下来抱在怀里：“劳烦替我给表哥带句话：先把门打开，账再慢慢查。我跑不了，也不打算跑。若怕我跑，派人跟车去姜府就是，总不能连我娘都不许见吧？”
二姑母顺势说：“我亲自押她回去。
你若不放心，就写下我的名字。”
亲卫僵持片刻，终于请来了管事。管事看了一眼门外越聚越多的人，咬牙让开路，还真派了两个人一路跟车。
钻进马车时，我的后背已经汗透。
春桃坐在我对面，替我拆头上的簪子。
拆到第三支时，簪尾勾住头发，疼得我倒吸一口凉气。
她眼眶一红：“小姐，世子不会真把您送去家庙吧？”
我心里一紧。
“谁跟你说的？”
“上月您得罪了温姑娘，世子就提过。
夫人没让我听，可我在门外听见了。”
我摸着腕上那圈被谢临舟捏出的红痕，忽然觉得，第十九章那场火并没有离我很远。
姜府正厅里，母亲李氏已经等着了。
她见我进门，第一句话却不是责骂。
“手伸出来。”
她捏住我的手腕，看见淤红，脸色沉了几分。
“谢临舟动的？”
“他不肯松手。”
“旁的地方呢？”
“没有。”
李氏这才松开手，目光落在我抱着的凤冠上：“是谁替你穿上的这身嫁衣？”
她手心有淡淡的草药香。穿来之前，我妈也总嫌我夜里不睡觉，隔三差五在手机上问我有没有好好吃饭。我想到那条没来得及回的消息，鼻子忽然有点酸。
“温梨。”
“你同她一起商量的？”
“她去刑部递状纸的事，你知道？”
“不知道。”
母亲盯着我看了半晌。我正怕她问“你是不是脑子坏了”，她却问：“春桃说，你让她收着一盅药茶。东西呢？”
我一怔。
“您怎么知道是药茶？”
“她回府报信时，连哭带说，把你交代的事说了个七七八八。”母亲伸出手，“先拿来。”
春桃把从温府一路护到侯府、又带回姜家的小布包放上桌。里面是封好的茶盅、余下的药粉，以及那块沾了粉的帕子。我看见茶盅，想起自己差一点就害了人，胃里又难受起来。
李氏看着那几样东西，过了好一会儿才说：“你今日若真害了她，娘护不住你，也不该护你。”
我低头：“我知道。”
她让春桃取来干净木盒，把几样东西分别包好、封存，准备明日请懂药的郎中辨认。
又让人给温府递话，姜家愿意赔罪，这些东西也不会私自销毁。
这几句话说完，我才敢坐下。
桌上还放着一封拆过的信。
落款是谢临舟，日期却是三天前。
我翻开看见“北河赈粮”几个字，心里顿时沉了。
信写得客客气气，说姜记商号三年前经手一批北河赈粮的水路转运。近日若刑部重查，请李氏把旧船票、脚行账目全部送到侯府，由他统一核对。
“他三天前就知道？”我问。
“他一直知道姜家走过那批船。”母亲说，“我原以为他是来提醒我。如今想来，他是想先把单据拿到手。”
“那您给了吗？”
“没给。”
她轻轻敲了敲桌边那只上锁的木匣。
“当年官府急着调粮，姜家替人雇船，脚钱也是照规矩收的。可船发走后，仓里回来的收条对不上。你爹在世时，便叫宋账房留了一份底。”
“宋账房呢？”
“去年病故。”
母亲摸了摸木匣上的锁。
她平时谈生意能让三个管事同时闭嘴，提到宋账房，声音却慢了下来。
“他死前求过我两次，说那些东西不该留。我没舍得烧，也没敢拿出去。”
“为什么？”
“因为一张票能救人，也能害人。”她看着我，“要是只交出自己手里这张，却不知道别人手里还有什么，怎么知道最后会害了谁？”
我想起自己举着一本书就以为能救温梨，忽然有点心虚。
门房忽然进来：“夫人，温姑娘求见。人已到后门。”
我猛地站起：“她还敢来？”
温梨是从绣坊旁边的小门进来的。
她换了一身素净衣裙，鞋帮上一道泥印还没干。
姜府的老门房跟在几步之外，神情比她还紧张。
李氏看着她：“你不是刚去了刑部？”
“状纸和账册已经收下了。刑部记了我的姓名，叫我留下可供传唤的住处。”温梨规规矩矩行了一礼，“我借姜府马车出了温家，过两条街就让车夫回去了，车牌也还给了他。我没有让他送我去刑部。来这里之前，我又绕了路。”
母亲冷着脸：“你把我女儿留在侯府做幌子时，倒没这么客气。”
温梨垂下眼：“是我算计了姜姑娘。她答应替我上花轿，没答应替我拖住世子，更没答应被人当成偷账的。”
我原本攒着一肚子骂，听她承认得这么痛快，倒是更生气了。
“你要递状纸为什么不告诉我？”
“怕你不同意。”
“我当然不会同意！”
“所以我没说。”
她抬起头，没躲。
“我知道不厚道。你要骂我，等会儿再骂。”温梨说，“我今天一定得来，是因为那本账牵出了姜记。我不想让你们从谢临舟口中听说这件事。”
“你还知道啊？”
“侯府那本旧账写着，腊月初九，姜记从水路运了八千石北河赈粮。”
李氏脸色变了：“腊月初九？”
温梨点头。
“不可能。”母亲的声音一下子紧了，“那年北河的航道，十一月底就封了。姜家的船明明是十一月十八日走的。”
“这两笔记的真是同一批粮？”我问。
“现在还不能断定。”母亲说，“所以才要找当年的船票和官仓记录。”
说完她便住了口，像是不小心把藏了三年的事说了出来。
温梨目光一动，却没有催她打开木匣。
“姜夫人，我不是来拿原件的。”温梨说，“我只想问，当年姜家的船究竟哪天离港，有没有另外留下凭证。”
母亲反问：“你想把姜家推到刑部面前？”
“姜记的名字已经被写进账里。”温梨说，“不查清楚，旁人照着那本账说事，我们连反驳的依据都没有。”
两个人隔着桌子对望，谁也不肯先退。
我插了一句：“先说清楚。姜家替人雇船，不等于姜家收了粮，更不等于知道粮最后去了哪儿，对吧？”
母亲转头看我：“自然。”
我望着温梨：“你递的那本账，只能证明有人把姜记写了进去，不能证明姜家真的在腊月初九运过粮。你想和我们一起查，就别把猜的当成已经查清的。”
温梨静了片刻。
“好。”她点头，“我以后把知道的和猜的分开说。”
她这声比先前轻得多。
我还没打算原谅她：“还有一件事。你得告诉我，侯府书房那本旧账究竟怎么到了你手里。”
温梨摇头：“现在不能说出那个人的名字。那人的家眷还在侯府。”
“你又瞒我？”
“这件事我得瞒。”她看着我，“你可以因此不帮我，可我不能为了让你信我，就拿别人的命冒险。”
我闭上嘴。
母亲看了温梨好一会儿，忽然把上锁的木匣往桌子中央推了推。
“坐下吧。”
“要谈，就把各自知道的账摊开来。”她说，“谁家的错，谁家担。但想拿我女儿换一条活路，门都没有。”
她从袖中取出钥匙。
铜锁轻轻响了一声。

annotations.explain: stop sb at ... 表示在某个位置把人拦下；stop sb from doing 才表示阻止做某事。
annotations.example: The guard stopped us at the entrance.

annotations.explain: stand in for sb 表示临时代替某人。这里不仅是穿了嫁衣，还意味着姜明月代替温梨进入婚礼现场。
annotations.example: She stood in for her sister at the ceremony.

annotations.explain: clutch 比 hold 更突出紧张时用力抓住、怕东西掉落。
annotations.example: She clutched her bag to her chest.

annotations.explain: everyone is talking / the whole town is talking 用夸张的集合主语表示流言传开；不要求字面上所有人都知道。
annotations.example: The whole town is talking about the wedding.

annotations.explain: at once 常用于命令或紧迫情境；也可表示“同时”，须根据上下文判断。
annotations.example: Come home at once.

annotations.explain: her voice rising ... 是独立主格式的伴随描写：主句说春桃抱着衣服，后面补充她说话时的状态。
annotations.example: She rushed inside, her hands shaking.

annotations.explain: low profile 在这里指尽量不惹人注意。
annotations.example: She tried to keep a low profile at the party.

annotations.phrase: hadn't even had time to change
annotations.meaning: 连换衣服的时间都没有
annotations.explain: not even have time to do sth 强调忙乱到连基本动作都来不及；两个 had 分别是过去完成时助动词和实义动词。
annotations.example: I hadn't even had time to eat.

annotations.explain: do nothing to help 表示非但无助于改善局面；这里用进行时加强当时的讽刺感。
annotations.example: His explanation did nothing to help.

annotations.phrase: What does the second part have to do with me?
annotations.meaning: 后面那件事跟我有什么关系？
annotations.explain: What does A have to do with B? 是质问两件事为何相关的常用说法。这里带有不满和自我辩解。
annotations.example: What does that rumor have to do with us?

annotations.phrase: You think the people spreading rumors care?
annotations.meaning: 你以为传闲话的人会在乎吗？
annotations.explain: You think ...? 省略 Do，口语中常带不耐烦或反驳；care 的宾语由语境省略。
annotations.example: You think anyone will believe that?

annotations.phrase: She couldn't have been more than fifteen or sixteen
annotations.explain: couldn’t have been more than ... 是回顾时的估计，强调年龄不会超过这个范围，并不是“她不可能曾经……”的字面否定。
annotations.example: He couldn't have been more than twenty at the time.

annotations.explain: look ready to do sth 表示从神情判断某动作即将发生。
annotations.example: He looked ready to argue.

annotations.explain: for the first time since + 事件/时间点：强调从某个起点到现在，首次发生某事。
annotations.example: For the first time since Monday, she smiled.

annotations.explain: barely 表示“几乎不”，语气比 only appeared a little 更自然紧凑。
annotations.example: He barely appeared in the first episode.

annotations.explain: along with 表示“连同、与……一起”，尤其用于人物或物品一并处理。
annotations.example: The letter was sent along with the documents.

annotations.explain: not bother to do 表示没有费心去做，语气常带埋怨。这里讽刺原著连春桃受罚的原因都不解释。
annotations.example: The report never bothered to explain why.

annotations.explain: head for + 地点是叙事中高频移动动词，比 go to 更带目标感。
annotations.example: We headed for the station.

annotations.explain: sheathed 表示剑尚在鞘中；不是拔剑攻击。
annotations.example: The guard held out his sheathed sword.

annotations.explain: block sb's path / block the way 描写物理阻拦，也可比喻有人妨碍计划。
annotations.example: A fallen tree blocked our path.

annotations.explain: for now 表示“眼下暂时”，暗示未来可能改变，与 forever 不同。
annotations.example: We'll stay here for now.

annotations.phrase: What's that got to do with me?
annotations.explain: What has ... got to do with ...? 是 have to do with 的英式/口语变式，用于质疑关联。
annotations.example: What's that got to do with our plan?

annotations.phrase: Our orders are to keep you here
annotations.meaning: 我们接到的命令是把你留在这里
annotations.explain: orders are to + 动词原形：正式地说明上级下达的任务；不是普通个人打算。
annotations.example: Our orders are to wait outside.

annotations.explain: without further + 名词常见于正式说明，further 是“进一步的”。
annotations.example: Do not proceed without further approval.

annotations.explain: take responsibility 通常是承担责任。此处说护卫不愿擅自放人、独自为后果担责，是叙述者对僵局的判断。
annotations.example: Nobody wanted to take responsibility for the mistake.

annotations.explain: 用于重新解释或点破上一段话的实际含义，小说旁白常带吐槽效果。
annotations.example: In other words, we have no choice.

annotations.explain: peer 常指费力、仔细地看，区别于一般的 look。
annotations.example: I peered through the window.

annotations.phrase: with two of my aunts standing beside it
annotations.explain: with + 名词 + doing 表示伴随情形，用于补充画面细节，不需要新建一个完整句子。
annotations.example: She entered with everyone watching her.

annotations.explain: 夸张地描写二婶说教没完没了；不是字面上的完全没有呼吸。
annotations.example: She talked for ten minutes without stopping for air.

annotations.phrase: lecture the original Jiang Mingyue about manners
annotations.meaning: 就礼数向原来的姜明月说教
annotations.explain: lecture sb about/on sth 可表示居高临下地训斥，不是大学“授课”。
annotations.example: Don't lecture me about being late.

annotations.meaning: 一个完全说得过去的理由
annotations.explain: perfectly good 是强调理由确实充分；这里是姜明月的自嘲：平时爱训人的二婶，这次倒真的有理由训她。
annotations.example: You have a perfectly good reason to leave.

annotations.explain: for once 表示与往常形成反差，这里突出二姑母平时没事也训人。
annotations.example: For once, he was early.

annotations.explain: raise one's voice 常为让别人听见或在争论时提高音量；raise 需带宾语 voice。
annotations.example: She raised her voice over the noise.

annotations.phrase: at the sight of me in red
annotations.explain: at the sight of ... 表示“看到……的一瞬间”引发即时反应。
annotations.example: He froze at the sight of the letter.

annotations.explain: face darkened 是情绪变化的描写，表示恼怒或不悦，不是肤色发生变化。
annotations.example: His face darkened when he heard the news.

annotations.explain: 在 What have you done this time? 中，this time 暗示对方过去也常闯祸，带责怪。
annotations.example: What did you break this time?

annotations.explain: get sb out of somewhere 是很常见的口语求助句式，重点是帮助脱离困境。
annotations.example: Please get me out of this room.

annotations.explain: round on someone 表示突然转向某人发怒或责问。
annotations.example: She rounded on the guard.

annotations.phrase: Since when does the Xie family get to detain an unmarried girl?
annotations.meaning: 谢家什么时候有权扣留未出嫁的姑娘了？
annotations.explain: Since when does ... get to ...? 是带有挑战意味的反问，质疑对方凭什么享有这种权力，而不是单纯询问起始时间。
annotations.example: Since when do you get to make that decision for me?

annotations.explain: fetch sb 既可指去带某人来，也可指取物品；比 call 在这里更突出“去请来”。
annotations.example: Fetch the doctor, please.

annotations.phrase: Does that mean she has to spend the night here
annotations.meaning: 难道这就意味着她得在这里过夜？
annotations.explain: Does that mean ...? 可以字面求解释，也可用来反驳不合理推论，本句属于后者。
annotations.example: Does that mean we have to start over?

annotations.phrase: pass a message to my cousin
annotations.explain: pass a message to sb / pass on a message 表示传话，不必亲自与对方交谈。
annotations.example: Could you pass a message to her?

annotations.explain: sort out sth / sort sth out 表示解决、整理混乱问题；sort accounts 不如 sort out accounts 自然。
annotations.example: We'll sort out the paperwork tomorrow.

annotations.explain: 现在进行时可以表达眼下的意图；not running away 在争执中否认对方假设。
annotations.example: I'm not avoiding you; I'm just busy.

annotations.phrase: Surely I'm still allowed to see my mother?
annotations.meaning: 总不至于连我娘都不准见吧？
annotations.explain: Surely ...? 是说话者认为答案理应为是的反问，语气可含施压。
annotations.example: Surely we can discuss this first?

annotations.explain: 反身代词 myself 强调“不假他人之手”，而非只是表示“我自己”。
annotations.example: I'll explain it to him myself.

annotations.explain: answer for sth 指为某事承担责任或接受追究，比 answer a question 更严肃。
annotations.example: Someone will have to answer for this mistake.

annotations.explain: 描写不情愿但不得不做出决定。
annotations.example: He gritted his teeth and agreed.

annotations.explain: standoff 在这里是僵持、对峙，指双方谁也不先退让；不是已经发生身体冲突。
annotations.example: After a brief standoff, the guard stepped aside.

annotations.explain: take one look at ... 常接即时反应，强调仅一眼就足以判断。
annotations.example: She took one look at the room and left.

annotations.explain: step aside 字面是站到一旁，语境里表示放行；亦可比喻让位。
annotations.example: The guard stepped aside to let us pass.

annotations.phrase: sent two men to follow the carriage
annotations.explain: send sb to do sth 表示安排某人执行任务，区别于 send sth to sb 寄送物品。
annotations.example: They sent an officer to investigate.

annotations.phrase: my back was soaked with sweat
annotations.explain: soaked with 表示完全湿透。
annotations.example: Her coat was soaked with rain.

annotations.phrase: By the time I climbed in
annotations.explain: by the time + 过去事件，通常表达另一状态到该时点已形成；此处汗早已湿透。
annotations.example: By the time we arrived, the shops had closed.

annotations.phrase: taking the pins out of my hair
annotations.meaning: 把簪子从头发里取下来
annotations.explain: take sth out of ... 是取出固定在某处的东西，也常见于 take a phone out of a bag。
annotations.example: She took a key out of her pocket.

annotations.explain: catch 可指东西意外挂住、卡住，不只表示“接住”。
annotations.example: My sleeve caught on the door handle.

annotations.explain: hiss 本义为嘶嘶作声，叙事中可描写疼痛时短促吸气或发声。
annotations.example: He hissed in pain as he stood up.

annotations.phrase: won't really send you to the family shrine, will he?
annotations.meaning: 他不会真把你送到家庙吧？
annotations.explain: 否定陈述句 + 肯定附加疑问 will he? 往往带担心并试图求得安慰。
annotations.example: She won't leave without us, will she?

annotations.explain: 胃部绷紧是焦虑感的身体化描写，不必字面译为胃在缩小。
annotations.example: My stomach tightened when I saw his name.

annotations.explain: offend sb 表示冒犯、得罪，不仅指触犯法律；be offended 则侧重感到被冒犯。
annotations.example: I didn't mean to offend you.

annotations.explain: 用 waiting for 暗示命运威胁，并非火有意识。
annotations.example: I was afraid of the trouble waiting for us.

annotations.explain: leave marks/bruises around/on ... 表示造成痕迹；这里过去完成时回顾更早的抓握。
annotations.example: The bracelet had left red marks on her skin.

annotations.explain: not seem so far away 描写预感危险正在逼近；not so + 形容词 表示程度变化。
annotations.example: The deadline suddenly didn't seem so far away.

annotations.phrase: was waiting in the Jiang residence's main hall
annotations.explain: 过去进行时 was waiting 展现人物进入场景时另一动作已持续。
annotations.example: My brother was waiting in the hall.

annotations.phrase: Her first words were not a scolding
annotations.meaning: 她开口第一句并不是责骂
annotations.explain: first words were ... 是写人物初次反应的简洁句式，scolding 可作名词“训斥”。
annotations.example: His first words were an apology.

annotations.explain: grow + 形容词表示状态逐渐变化，如 grow quiet/cold/serious。
annotations.example: Her expression grew serious.

annotations.explain: 过去时中的 wouldn’t 常表示当时拒绝或不愿做某事；这里并不是对未来行为的预测。
annotations.example: I asked him to stop, but he wouldn't listen.

annotations.explain: anywhere else 常与疑问、否定搭配，问“是否还有别处”。
annotations.example: Does it hurt anywhere else?

annotations.phrase: Only then did she release me
annotations.explain: Only then 置于句首触发部分倒装：Only then + did + 主语 + 动词原形。
annotations.example: Only then did I understand his warning.

annotations.explain: one's eyes fell on ... 是小说常用注意力转换描写，不表示眼睛真的掉落。
annotations.example: Her eyes fell on the open letter.

annotations.phrase: Her palms carried a faint scent of herbs
annotations.meaning: 她手心带着淡淡的草药香
annotations.explain: carry a scent 描写某人身上或物体散发气味。
annotations.example: The room carried a faint scent of tea.

annotations.explain: 形容想哭或强忍情绪时的生理感觉。
annotations.example: My throat tightened when I saw her.

annotations.explain: end up + 地点/状态指“最终落到某处或某种处境”，常带意料之外。
annotations.example: We ended up in the wrong room.

annotations.explain: stay up 指不睡觉、继续醒着；与 get up 起床相区别。
annotations.example: I stayed up late reading.

annotations.explain: every few + 复数名词表示大约每隔几次/几天，不等于 every day。
annotations.example: She called me every few days.

annotations.phrase: asking if I was eating properly
annotations.explain: ask if + 完整从句表示询问“是否……”，不必直接说 yes/no。
annotations.example: He asked if I had slept well.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时 had never answered 相对于回忆时点，突出尚未完成且无法挽回的事。
annotations.example: I remembered the email I'd never answered.

annotations.phrase: going to the Ministry of Punishments with a complaint
annotations.explain: go to + 地点 + with + 物品，说明带什么去；with a complaint 这里是携带正式申诉文件。
annotations.example: She went to the office with a written complaint.

annotations.explain: brace for 指预料会有难受或严厉的事情发生。
annotations.example: I was bracing for bad news.

annotations.phrase: studied me for a long moment
annotations.explain: study sb 可表示认真观察其神情、反应，不是“学习某个人”。
annotations.example: She studied his face for a moment.

annotations.phrase: Are you out of your mind?
annotations.explain: 固定口语，表示强烈震惊或责备；不能逐词译成“离开自己的头脑”。
annotations.example: Are you out of your mind? That's dangerous!

annotations.meaning: 好不容易向我说清楚了
annotations.explain: manage to do 表示在困难中仍设法完成，常强调结果确实发生。
annotations.example: She managed to explain what happened.

annotations.explain: Give it here 是直接口语命令，比 Please hand it to me 更短促、更有长辈或权威语气。
annotations.example: Give it here; I'll carry it.

annotations.phrase: The sight of them turned my stomach
annotations.meaning: 看到那些东西我胃里一阵难受
annotations.explain: turn someone’s stomach 可表示恶心，也可表示强烈的不安。
annotations.example: The smell turned my stomach.

annotations.explain: all the way 强调全过程或很长的距离，带有“从头到尾”的意味。
annotations.example: We walked all the way home.

annotations.phrase: Inside were the sealed tea bowl
annotations.explain: 地点副词 Inside 提前形成完全倒装，结构为 Inside + 谓语 + 主语；常用于呈现物品。
annotations.example: Inside was a small silver key.

annotations.explain: with one's own hands 强调责任直接落在自己身上，尤其适合愧疚语境。
annotations.example: He built the table with his own hands.

annotations.phrase: I couldn't have protected you. And I shouldn't have.
annotations.meaning: 我保不住你，也不该保你
annotations.explain: couldn’t have done 表示在那种假设情形下做不到；shouldn’t have 则加上一层道德判断：即使做得到也不应该包庇。
annotations.example: I couldn't have hidden the truth, and I shouldn't have tried.

annotations.explain: at last 表示一段等待或犹豫后终于发生，比 finally 在情感场景更具叙事停顿。
annotations.example: At last, she spoke.

annotations.explain: 分别封存意味着各项物证不混放，副词修饰 wrapped and sealed。
annotations.example: Keep the samples separately.

annotations.explain: have sb do sth 是使役结构，请/让某人做某事；不是 have sb to do。
annotations.example: I'll have a mechanic check the car.

annotations.explain: would not 是叙述过去时点里对未来行动的承诺（间接引语中的 will → would）；destroy the evidence 是“销毁证据”。这句只表明保留物证，不表示已经证明指控。
annotations.example: They promised they would not destroy the records.

annotations.phrase: sent word to the Wen family
annotations.explain: send word (to sb) 是固定搭配“传话、通知”，不一定有书面信件。
annotations.example: Send word when you arrive safely.

annotations.phrase: Only after that did I dare sit down
annotations.meaning: 直到那之后我才敢坐下
annotations.explain: Only after ... 置于句首触发主句部分倒装；dare 在此是普通实义动词。
annotations.example: Only after the meeting did I relax.

annotations.phrase: An opened letter lay on the table
annotations.meaning: 一封拆过的信放在桌上
annotations.explain: lay 是 lie（躺、放置）的过去式；与 lay（放下、产卵）的现在式同形，容易混淆。
annotations.example: A small envelope lay on the floor.

annotations.explain: dated + 时间 可指文件标注的日期，不能误读为“约会”。
annotations.example: The letter was dated June 12.

annotations.meaning: 那几个字赫然映入我眼里
annotations.explain: stare back at someone 带有醒目、令人不安的修辞效果。
annotations.example: The warning stared back at me.

annotations.explain: one's heart sinks/sank 是常见情绪惯用表达，指坏消息带来的失落或不安。
annotations.example: My heart sank when I saw the bill.

annotations.explain: unfailingly 强调始终、一贯。
annotations.example: His letters were unfailingly polite.

annotations.phrase: was to send all the old boat tickets and transport accounts
annotations.meaning: 须将旧船票和运输账目全部送交
annotations.explain: be to do 在正式书信或命令中可表示预定安排或要求；这里暗示谢临舟以客气措辞要求姜家交出凭证。
annotations.example: All records were to be delivered by Friday.

annotations.phrase: If the Ministry reopened the case
annotations.meaning: 如果刑部重新调查案件
annotations.explain: reopen a case 指把旧案重新拿出来调查，不是重新打开一个实体箱子。
annotations.example: The police decided to reopen the case.

annotations.explain: himself 加强他本人直接处理，不代表独自一人。
annotations.example: The director reviewed the records herself.

annotations.explain: 陈述句语序 + 问号是口语里的回声式疑问，常表达惊讶和怀疑。
annotations.example: You knew about this yesterday?

annotations.explain: 强调取得物品，语境里可能含有控制证据的目的。
annotations.example: She wanted to get hold of the file.

annotations.phrase: I thought he was warning me
annotations.meaning: 我原以为他是在提醒我
annotations.explain: I thought ... 描写之前判断，现在往往被事实推翻；此处 implied but now I suspect otherwise。
annotations.example: I thought you were joking.

annotations.phrase: She tapped a locked wooden chest
annotations.meaning: 她轻敲一个上锁的木匣
annotations.explain: tap sth 可表示轻敲以引起注意，不一定是在敲门。
annotations.example: She tapped the table twice.

annotations.phrase: the receipts that came back from the granary didn't match
annotations.meaning: 粮仓回来的收据对不上
annotations.explain: didn’t match 指不同来源的记录彼此不一致。这里发现的是账目疑点，尚不能直接证明谁造假或侵吞粮食。
annotations.example: The delivery records didn't match the invoices.

annotations.explain: be desperate to do sth 指非常急切、迫切，不一定是“绝望地”。
annotations.example: They were desperate to leave before dark.

annotations.phrase: was paid the proper transport fee
annotations.explain: was paid 是被动语态；proper 在这里是合规、按规矩，而不是“适当的性格”。
annotations.example: The contractor was paid the agreed fee.

annotations.phrase: While your father was still alive
annotations.explain: while + 时间状语从句设定事情发生的历史背景；still 表示当时尚处于该状态。
annotations.example: While my grandmother was alive, she kept a diary.

annotations.explain: keep copies of ... 指留存副本以便核对，和 keep the original 原件不同。
annotations.example: Please keep copies of all receipts.

annotations.phrase: ran a finger over the lock
annotations.explain: run a finger over/across sth 是小说里的触觉动作描写，不是跑步。
annotations.example: She ran a finger across the old photograph.

annotations.meaning: 能一下让三个管事都闭嘴
annotations.explain: silence 作动词表示使某人不再说话；at once 在这里是“同时”，与前文“立刻”不同。
annotations.example: One sharp look silenced the room at once.

annotations.explain: couldn’t bring oneself to do 表示心理上不愿或做不到。
annotations.example: I couldn't bring myself to throw it away.

annotations.explain: get rid of 是固定搭配“摆脱、扔掉、处置”；rid 不单独按日常动词使用。
annotations.example: We need to get rid of these old boxes.

annotations.phrase: didn't dare show them to anyone
annotations.meaning: 不敢把它们拿给任何人看
annotations.explain: not dare (to) do 表示没有勇气；show sth to sb 是展示给某人。
annotations.example: I didn't dare tell her the truth.

annotations.phrase: a single ticket can save someone—or ruin them
annotations.meaning: 一张凭证可能救人，也可能害人
annotations.explain: save / ruin 的强烈对照说明同一张凭证既可能还人清白，也可能被用来指控别人，解释李氏为何不敢轻易交出旧票据。
annotations.example: A single document can change the case.

annotations.meaning: 交出你手里的那份凭据
annotations.explain: hand over 是交出、移交，带权利或控制权转移；这里强调单方面交证物的风险。
annotations.example: He refused to hand over the files.

annotations.explain: tell 在这里是辨别、判断，不是“告诉”；How can you tell? 是高频问法。
annotations.example: How can you tell if the letter is real?

annotations.phrase: I'd thought I could save Wen Li
annotations.meaning: 我原以为自己能救温梨
annotations.explain: I'd thought 与突然醒悟形成反差：过去先前的笃定现在受到了挑战。
annotations.example: I'd thought the problem was simple.

annotations.explain: rather + 形容词表示“相当、有点”，语气因场合而变；这里是自嘲。
annotations.example: I felt rather foolish afterward.

annotations.phrase: A servant appeared at the door
annotations.explain: appear 可直接接地点状语，小说常借此快速引入消息或人物。
annotations.example: A messenger appeared at the window.

annotations.meaning: 她居然还有脸、有胆量去
annotations.explain: have the nerve to 带有说话人的气愤和不满。
annotations.example: He had the nerve to ask for more.

annotations.explain: shoot to one's feet 固定表达“突然起身”，shoot 不表示开枪。
annotations.example: She shot to her feet in surprise.

annotations.explain: streak of + 物质/颜色指狭长条状痕迹；fresh 表示刚留下不久。
annotations.example: There was a streak of paint on his sleeve.

annotations.explain: a pace 是一步的距离；several paces behind 比 a little behind 更有可视化空间感。
annotations.example: He walked several paces behind us.

annotations.explain: 比较句中的 did 代替前面已知的动词 looked，避免重复；不是“做了”某事。
annotations.example: He looked more surprised than I did.

annotations.explain: regard sb + 副词常表示带评价地打量；coolly 是冷淡、克制，不是凉爽。
annotations.example: He regarded the stranger coolly.

annotations.phrase: asked for an address where I could be summoned
annotations.meaning: 要求留下日后可传唤我的地址
annotations.explain: where I could be summoned 修饰 address，说明需要一个正式联系地点；被登记、可传唤不等于已经获准立案审判或证实指控。
annotations.example: The office asked for an address where she could be reached.

annotations.explain: for the record 可表示正式登记或说明以供记录；在这里指官署收下材料登记，不代表审判事实成立。
annotations.example: Her statement was put on the record.

annotations.explain: properly 说明符合礼节规矩，与 simply bowed 的中性叙述不同。
annotations.example: He greeted the guests properly.

annotations.explain: roundabout 形容路线不直接、曲折；可用于交通，也可形容委婉说话。
annotations.example: We took a roundabout route to avoid traffic.

annotations.explain: not nearly so + 形容词强调差得远；这里是李氏用反话指责温梨。
annotations.example: He wasn't nearly so calm yesterday.

annotations.meaning: 作为转移注意力的幌子
annotations.explain: distraction 不只表示娱乐消遣，也可指故意转移他人注意。
annotations.example: They used the noise as a distraction.

annotations.explain: took advantage of 这里指不公平地利用对方。
annotations.example: She took advantage of his trust.

annotations.meaning: 拖住世子，让他无暇顾及别处
annotations.explain: keep sb occupied = 使某人一直忙着或分神；occupied 不限于房间被占用。
annotations.example: Keep the children occupied while we work.

annotations.explain: accuse sb of doing sth 是固定结构，变被动为 be accused of doing sth。
annotations.example: She was accused of hiding the letter.

annotations.phrase: Hearing her admit it so readily only made me angrier
annotations.meaning: 听她承认得这么干脆，我反而更生气
annotations.explain: only made me + 比较级 说明结果事与预期相反：对方坦白并没有平息怒火，反而加重了情绪。
annotations.example: His apology only made her more upset.

annotations.phrase: I'd spent the whole ride thinking of
annotations.explain: spend + 时间 + doing sth 是时间用法；the whole ride 把“乘车全程”当时间跨度。
annotations.example: I spent the evening thinking about it.

annotations.explain: yell at sb 带责骂意味；yell to sb 偏指隔远处大声喊，介词决定语气。
annotations.example: He yelled at me for being late.

annotations.explain: file a complaint 是行政/法律语境的固定搭配，file 作动词“正式提交”，不是归档文件夹。
annotations.example: She filed a complaint with the school.

annotations.explain: you'd = you would，这里是站在过去视角预测“你会不会同意”，而不是 had 的过去完成时。
annotations.example: I thought you'd be angry.

annotations.explain: I'd have + 过去分词是 would have 的缩写，表示在假设过去情形下本会怎样；此处否认曾经同意。
annotations.example: If you'd asked, I'd have said no.

annotations.phrase: That's why I didn't tell you
annotations.explain: That's why ... 用来说明结果的原因；与 That's because ... 引入原因的方向不同。
annotations.example: I was ill. That's why I stayed home.

annotations.explain: meet someone’s eyes 是直视并不躲闪。
annotations.example: He looked up and met my eyes.

annotations.explain: have to + 动词是客观或主观紧迫需要；过去式 had to 对应叙事时间。
annotations.example: I had to see you before leaving.

annotations.phrase: hear about it from Xie Linzhou
annotations.meaning: 从谢临舟那里才得知此事
annotations.explain: hear about sth from sb 突出消息来源；不等于 hear sb 直接听到某人说话。
annotations.example: I didn't want to hear it from a stranger.

annotations.explain: 反话，实际表达不满，语调和上下文决定含义。
annotations.example: How thoughtful of you to remember now.

annotations.phrase: on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month
annotations.explain: on + 具体日期；the ninth day of ... 是文学叙事中表达农历日子的写法。
annotations.example: The meeting fell on the fifth day of the month.

annotations.explain: sharply 修饰说话方式，暗示急促、紧绷或斥责，不能机械译为“尖锐地说”。
annotations.example: "Stop," she said sharply.

annotations.phrase: Are those records even talking about the same shipment?
annotations.meaning: 那些记录说的真是同一批货吗？
annotations.explain: even 放在疑问句中强化怀疑。姜明月提醒大家：日期冲突前，要先确认比较对象是否相同。
annotations.example: Are we even looking at the same document?

annotations.explain: shipment 指一批运输中的货物，不必指整个航运行业；辨别 same shipment 是证据推理关键。
annotations.example: Are these invoices for the same shipment?

annotations.explain: yet 表示截至当前时点仍未得知，暗示未来可以查清。
annotations.example: We don't know the answer yet.

annotations.phrase: as if she'd just revealed something
annotations.explain: as if + 从句描述观察者主观推断，不等于事实已经得到证实。
annotations.example: She froze as if she'd heard a noise.

annotations.phrase: made no move toward the chest
annotations.meaning: 没有朝木匣伸手或采取动作
annotations.explain: make no move to/toward ... 表示有意识地不采取行动，突出了温梨在克制。
annotations.example: He made no move to open the door.

annotations.explain: not come to do sth 是否定来的目的，常用于先澄清动机。
annotations.example: I didn't come to argue.

annotations.meaning: 是否还有其他记录留存
annotations.explain: whether 引导间接疑问；survive 可指文献、物件留存下来，而不只是生物存活。
annotations.example: We don't know whether the letters survived.

annotations.phrase: drag the Jiang family before the Ministry
annotations.explain: drag sb before ... 用带强制感的比喻，含有让人被迫接受审查的负面评价。
annotations.example: He feared being dragged before the committee.

annotations.phrase: we'll have nothing to challenge them with
annotations.meaning: 我们就拿不出东西反驳他们
annotations.explain: challenge 在这里是质疑或反驳指控；with 后置，指反驳时依靠的证据，而不是挑战某个人的地位。
annotations.example: We need documents to challenge that claim with.

annotations.explain: use sth against sb 指把信息或证据作为攻击、施压或指控的工具。
annotations.example: Don't give them anything they can use against you.

annotations.explain: not give an inch 表示在争执中丝毫不让步。
annotations.example: Neither side would give an inch.

annotations.explain: cut in 是固定动词短语，表示中途插话或插入谈话；区别 cut off 使人说不下去。
annotations.example: "Wait," she cut in.

annotations.explain: before we go any further 是讨论中要求先澄清前提的高频句式。
annotations.example: Before we go any further, let's check the dates.

annotations.phrase: doesn't mean our family received the grain
annotations.meaning: 并不意味着姜家收过这批粮
annotations.explain: A doesn't mean B 用于纠正不成立的逻辑推断；句中强调“雇船≠收粮”。
annotations.example: A high price doesn't mean better quality.

annotations.explain: end up 表示最终的去向或结局；这里的 where 是嵌入式疑问，语序不倒装。
annotations.example: Nobody knows where the money ended up.

annotations.explain: Of course not 是完整的否定回答，比简单的 No 更强调对方的理解完全正确。
annotations.example: "Does that prove guilt?" "Of course not."

annotations.phrase: don't present a guess as a fact
annotations.explain: 关键不是抽象的“别乱猜”，而是区分“姜记名字出现在账簿”与“姜记实际参与了可疑运粮”；前者尚不能证明后者。
annotations.example: Don't present a guess as a fact.

annotations.phrase: doesn't prove our boats carried grain
annotations.meaning: 并不能证明姜家的船确实运了粮
annotations.explain: prove (that) ... 需要支持事实成立的证据；出现在账簿与实际发生不是一回事。
annotations.example: The photo doesn't prove he was there.

annotations.explain: from now on 指从此刻开始持续实施新的做法，不是指过去一段时间。
annotations.example: From now on, I'll tell you the truth.

annotations.phrase: I wasn't ready to forgive her
annotations.explain: be ready to do sth 是“准备好做某事”。not ready to forgive 表示情绪上尚无法原谅，留下未来改变的可能，而不是永远拒绝。
annotations.example: I am not ready to talk about it yet.

annotations.explain: 用于谈话即将结束或转换话题时追加重要问题，口语极常见。
annotations.example: One more thing—where is the key?

annotations.phrase: get out of the marquis's study and into your hands
annotations.meaning: 从侯府书房出来、到了你手里
annotations.explain: get out of A and into B 用空间移动描写东西如何被转交；这里隐含来源疑问。
annotations.example: How did the file get into your hands?

annotations.phrase: I can't name the person who helped me
annotations.meaning: 不能说出帮助我的那个人是谁
annotations.explain: name sb 可作动词“公开说出姓名”；这里不能告知身份并不等于没有人帮助。
annotations.example: She refused to name her source.

annotations.phrase: Their family is still inside the marquis's residence
annotations.explain: their 可指性别未知或不愿透露的单数人物（singular they）；这里避免通过代词暴露身份。
annotations.example: Someone left their umbrella here.

annotations.phrase: You're keeping another secret from me?
annotations.explain: keep a secret from sb 指向某人隐瞒秘密；陈述语序加问号突出责问。
annotations.example: You've been keeping this from me?

annotations.explain: win trust 指通过行动逐步获得信任。
annotations.example: It takes time to win someone's trust.

annotations.explain: hold sb's gaze 比 meet sb's eyes 更强调目光没有移开，常传达决心。
annotations.example: She held his gaze without blinking.

annotations.explain: risk + 名词或 risk doing sth；risk someone's life 强调造成严重后果的可能性。
annotations.example: He refused to risk another person's life.

annotations.meaning: 仅仅为了赢得你的信任
annotations.explain: just to do sth 可表达“不惜……只为……”并批评目的不值得代价。
annotations.example: I won't lie just to impress them.

annotations.explain: 此处是强硬驳斥某种打算，不是中性的再考虑。
annotations.example: If you think I'll agree, think again.

annotations.phrase: put every account we know about on the table
annotations.meaning: 把掌握的账目都摊开来
annotations.explain: put sth on the table 同时有物理放上桌与公开讨论之意，本句故意呼应两层含义。
annotations.example: Let's put all the options on the table.

annotations.phrase: Whoever is responsible will answer for it
annotations.explain: whoever 引导名词性从句作主语；answer for it 是承担责任，不只是解释。
annotations.example: Whoever broke it should pay for it.

annotations.phrase: buy their way out with my daughter's life
annotations.meaning: 拿我女儿的命换一条退路
annotations.explain: buy one's way out of sth 原指用钱解决困境，这里比喻牺牲别人换自己脱身。
annotations.example: He tried to buy his way out of trouble.

annotations.phrase: drew a key from her sleeve
annotations.explain: draw sth from ... 在文学叙事中可表示抽出、取出，比 take out 更有动作画面；不是画画。
annotations.example: He drew a letter from his pocket.

annotations.phrase: The brass lock gave a soft click.
annotations.explain: give a click 表示发出“咔嗒”声，动词 give 在这里是发出声音的搭配；短促响声作为章末动作，故意悬置木匣内证据。
annotations.example: The latch gave a faint click.

scenes.title: 侯府门前
scenes.alt: 姜明月穿着红嫁衣抱着凤冠，在侯府门前面对拦路亲卫与据理力争的长辈。

scenes.title: 归途马车
scenes.alt: 回姜府的马车里，春桃小心替姜明月拆下发簪，姜明月腕上有红痕。

scenes.title: 母亲察觉伤痕
scenes.alt: 姜府温暖的室内，李氏握住姜明月的手腕，察看刚留下的红痕。

scenes.title: 小心封存证物
scenes.alt: 木桌上，茶盅与纸包等物品正被逐件妥善收起。

scenes.title: 温梨登门
scenes.alt: 身着浅青绿衣裙的温梨走进姜府，与姜明月和李氏隔门相对，气氛凝重。

scenes.title: 上锁的木匣
scenes.alt: 烛光下，一只雕花木匣尚未开启，钥匙已取出，三人凝神注视。
